mixed_toc_regions.preserve_prefix_exact:
How to use this volume
Reading route. Exact packet coordinates and residue selectors lead to weighted inversion and
rational walk series. Lattice gluing then gives separation weights and precision delays. Smith con-
gruences and operator defects connect these formulas to finite computation.
Companions. The worked plates illustrate the constructions of this chapter. The formal companion
in the back matter distinguishes the chapter-wide correspondence from the foundational 25-row
walkthrough, with explicit evidence and scope.
Overview
A complete family of idempotents gives exact coordinates, but a single family does not record
scale or integral visibility. We study towers in which every coarse idempotent is the sum of its fine
descendants. The coordinate changes are invertible and coherent, and every operator block is the
sum of its refined blocks. Residue selectors give a model over arbitrary rings. When roots of unity
are available they agree with character averages, and coprime moduli factor through the Chinese re-
mainder theorem. In a complete filtered algebra, a diagonal operator plus positive weight transfers
has an inverse obtained by summing admissible weighted paths. The formula truncates exactly at
finite precision, while finite transfer graphs have rational path series. For a rational spectral decom-
position over a discrete valuation ring, resultants give denominator bounds. The exact denominator
is the largest Smith exponent of the lattice gluing module. This yields a necessary and sufficient pre-
cision delay, monotonicity under refinement, and a full congruence solving formula. We close with
exact formulas for the propagation of a coarsening defect through powers, resolvents, holomorphic
functions, exponentials, and multilevel towers.
The exposition distinguishes general written proofs, formal specifications, and finite computational
examples. The worked plates supply concrete models. The formal companion identifies the exact dec-
larations and hypotheses that support each mapped statement.

mixed_toc_regions.preserve_prefix_exact:
How to use this volume
Begin with typed edge words and exact coordinate transport. A chosen connection introduces
defects, holonomy, and packet obstruction witnesses. Part II develops nonlinear packet jets, tree
expansions, correction complexes, filtered lifting, elimination, and smooth transport.
Part I develops the finite algebraic core under its declaration-level formal contract. Part II gives
the nonlinear and analytic development with ordinary proofs. The accompanying formal develop-
ment verifies exact nonlinear coordinates, continuous packet jets on actual projector ranges, and
the decorated composition and structural support laws in Lean. The integral Taylor remainder
and the later analytic and obstruction results retain their ordinary proof status. Formal coverage
stays attached to the identified declarations. The visual atlas at the end of this volume provides
twenty-four worked plates. The separate Lean guide explains the formal contract and its evidence.
Overview
Finite projector packets turn linear transfer into typed walks and arbitrary maps into exact co-
ordinate representations. Canonical coordinate transport satisfies an exact cocycle law. A chosen
connection can fail to compose, producing holonomy and packet obstruction witnesses. Nonlinear
packet jets lead to higher composition, convergent rooted tree expansions, graded operations, and
nonlinear refinement defects. A specified correction map produces a canonical cokernel obstruction.
Relative exact sequences, mapping cones, Hilbert splitting, nonlinear correction, and filtered lift-
ing describe how these obstructions behave. Exact elimination produces Schur formulas, and finite
transport reduces gluing to fundamental cycle holonomy. For smooth orthogonal packet families,
direct packet rotations converge in operator norm to canonical unitary transport. The finite formal
contract and the broader ordinary proof development retain their separate scopes throughout.
The chapter presents the mathematical development together with worked examples, a visual atlas, and
a separate guide to the formal proof evidence. The packet norm estimate distinguishes the actual range
jet from its ambient extension. The support statements keep external packet profiles and intermediate
composition witnesses explicitly typed. The formal companion gives the exact source and scope of each
formal verification.

able in the finalization environment.
